court: Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit

issues.label: Scope and standard of review
issues.why: The court must determine what agency decision it reviews and under what deferential or de novo standards.

issues.label: Substantial evidence review of credibility
issues.why: Adverse credibility findings are reviewed for substantial evidence and drive the entire outcome.

issues.label: Basis for adverse credibility determination
issues.why: Court must assess whether discrepancies in positions and dates support the adverse credibility finding under the REAL ID Act totality standard.

issues.label: Materiality of inconsistencies
issues.why: Under 8 U.S.C. 1158(b)(1)(B)(iii), inconsistencies need not go to the heart of the claim but their significance still matters.

issues.label: Pro se litigant considerations
issues.why: The IJ's duty to develop the record fully for an unrepresented respondent may affect the fairness of the credibility findings.

issues.label: Corroboration requirement propriety
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether the IJ properly required corroborating evidence and gave notice and opportunity to provide it.

issues.label: Independent weight of non-testimonial evidence
issues.why: Court must determine whether documentary evidence independently established eligibility apart from discredited testimony.

issues.label: Removability determination
issues.why: The finding of removability for lacking a valid entry document must be supported.

issues.label: Asylum eligibility—nexus
issues.why: Court must consider whether persecution was on account of a protected ground: political opinion, ethnicity (Tajik), or particular social group.

issues.label: Particular social group cognizability
issues.why: Former Afghan government security personnel must qualify as a cognizable particular social group.

issues.label: Past persecution and presumption
issues.why: Prior imprisonment and torture may establish past persecution creating a rebuttable presumption of future fear.

issues.label: Well-founded fear of future persecution
issues.why: Taliban arrest warrants and searches bear on objective and subjective fear of future harm.

issues.label: Government or uncontrollable persecutor
issues.why: Whether the Taliban, as the controlling authority, constitutes a persecutor the government cannot or will not control.

issues.label: Internal relocation feasibility
issues.why: Whether Eqbal could reasonably relocate within Afghanistan to avoid Taliban persecution.

issues.label: Asylum bars and one-year filing deadline
issues.why: Court should consider whether statutory bars or the one-year deadline affect asylum eligibility.

issues.label: Withholding of removal—clear probability
issues.why: Withholding requires the higher clear-probability standard, assessed separately from asylum.

issues.label: CAT protection analysis
issues.why: CAT requires independent assessment of likelihood of torture with government acquiescence, regardless of credibility of other claims.

issues.label: Effect of credibility finding on CAT
issues.why: Court must determine whether CAT claim can survive on country conditions evidence despite adverse credibility.

issues.label: Country conditions evidence
issues.why: Objective evidence of Taliban treatment of former officials and Tajiks must be weighed independently.

issues.label: Whether remand is warranted
issues.why: Court must decide if legal errors require remand rather than outright grant or denial.
